details: For every finite binary class, the degeneracy of its 1-inclusion graph is at most its effective range.
proof: Every induced subgraph of the 1-inclusion graph has all degrees at most \mathrm E(\mathcal H), because an incident edge uses a distinct effective coordinate. Its minimum degree is at most this value, and maximizing those minima over induced subgraphs gives the claimed degeneracy bound.
name: Effective Range / Degeneracy
witness_verification: For #classes/halfintervals with n>=4, the established endpoint values or bounds, in parameter order, are $n-1$ and $1$. The first parameter divided by one plus the second tends to infinity. Thus no reverse affine-linear bound holds. See the database-owned endpoint value proofs.
